System

Elite phases, boss telegraphs and instanced dungeons

A small co-op dungeon is an independently allocated zone instance with a declared party roster, encounter state and recovery policy. Boss phases and telegraphs are server decisions; matching does not appear automatically because a dedicated server exists.

Scope and player interaction

A small co-op dungeon is an independently allocated zone instance with a declared party roster, encounter state and recovery policy. Boss phases and telegraphs are server decisions; matching does not appear automatically because a dedicated server exists.

StageMeaning
First integration: Phase18committed; full feature contract may include explicitly staged later extensions
EvidenceAuthored implementation specification; no native/Blueprint/backend runtime verified

UI state machine

Queued → Reserved → Traveling → Active → BossPhaseOne → BossPhaseTwo → Defeated → Completed → Recovering

WBP_DungeonFinder observes results from URPGDungeonInstanceComponent. Pending is not Accepted. Close/cancel clears local focus and stale callbacks, but cannot undo an already committed backend command.

Definitions, fields and units

Canonical definition: DA_Dungeon_SluiceVault. Stable IDs, quantities, seconds and centimeters are validated by the owner, not inferred from translated labels or sprites.

Field / rule
DungeonDefinitionId and InstanceId; max party size and level/quest gates
ReservationRoster and PartyRevision: immutable admission snapshot or explicit update
EncounterState/PhaseId/PhaseRevision: server-owned, persisted at chosen checkpoints
TelegraphSpec: shape/radius/direction/start/end and safe areas
BossDefeatId and per-character reward entitlement: unique per instance/encounter generation
InstanceExpiry/CheckpointId: recovery policy; lockouts disabled initially

C++ / Blueprint / backend ownership

LayerResponsibility
URPGDungeonInstanceComponentImplement the native validated request/state lifecycle described below; native runtime state is not editable by UMG.
Blueprint/Data AssetsTune the declared defaults and visual/asset assignments. Keep definition references EditDefaultsOnly/BlueprintReadOnly; cosmetic hooks cannot grant rewards.
Zone serverValidate live actor ownership, range/LOS, alive/action state, cooldown/tool/target rules and current session epoch where relevant.
BackendFor durable changes, revalidate trusted catalog/revision/ownership and commit records/source claims/receipt atomically. Read-only/cosmetic features have no durable mutation.
WBP_DungeonFinderLocal observer/requester. Create only for local player; bind once, refresh immediately, unbind on teardown.

Custom command contracts

These names are project custom APIs or backend proposals, not existing Unreal/PaperZD nodes. Economic/backend requests are asynchronous; Pending resolves through the same command ID. Pure local queries are synchronous unless noted.

Command / result
RequestDungeonEntry(CommandId, DungeonId, PartyId) -> Reservation|RequirementsFailed|NoCapacity
AdmitInstanceMember(Ticket, CharacterId) -> Accepted|NotInRoster
AdvanceBossPhase(VerifiedHealthThreshold) -> PhaseChanged|AlreadyApplied
CompleteDungeon(DefeatReceipt) -> Completed|Pending
RejoinDungeon(CharacterId, InstanceId) -> Admission|Expired|RecoveryHub

End-to-end command and observation flow

  1. Party leader requests SluiceVault; backend validates roster/revision, requirements and available instance capacity and reserves a server.
  2. Each member receives their own identity-bound transfer ticket; one player failure does not cause whole-server travel of unrelated players.
  3. Instance initializes registered encounters and checkpoint. Boss health thresholds/time rules select phases and publish telegraph state before impact.
  4. Server validates all melee/projectile/area hits; telegraph graphics cannot cause damage, and low visual settings must retain gameplay-critical shape cues.
  5. Boss defeat creates a unique durable encounter/reward receipt and completion fact for quests; loot rights use the declared party eligibility snapshot.
  6. Reconnect returns to an active reserved instance when valid. Server crash recovers from durable checkpoint under a documented reset policy with existing reward entitlements preserved.

Editor configuration and real consumers

  1. Author DA_Dungeon_SluiceVault with entrance/exit IDs, four-member limit, checkpoint and boss definitions. Create L_SluiceVault as a graybox interior with navigation and camera-occlusion tests.
  2. Create DA_Enemy_SluiceKeeper with two phases: cone sweep then alternating water-lane area effects; all art/meshes/VFX are acquisition/authoring tasks.
  3. Place BP_DungeonController and encounter spawners; connect their state to the backend instance record and zone transfer system.
  4. Build WBP_DungeonFinder with party readiness, requirements, queue/reservation status and cancel. Start a simple explicit party-entry queue before automated role matching.
  5. Reopen party/quest/loot/recovery components to handle instance identity and reconnect; test wipe/reset after one already-rewarded encounter.

Reopen Phase18 integration entries after creating the assets. Test fixture: L_SluiceVault / Boss_SluiceKeeper / Party_ABCD. No later-phase runtime dependency should be activated before its recorded integration phase.

Failure, contention and recovery acceptance

Test stimulus and expected result
Party roster changes after reservation -> require refresh or explicit allowed member update; no unauthorized entrant.
Boss threshold processed twice -> one phase transition/cue sequence.
Server restart after boss reward -> no second loot/quest completion.
Player disconnects during telegraph -> server simulation continues; rejoin obeys safe checkpoint policy.
Instance expired -> return to safe hub with preserved durable inventory/quests.

Repeat the success route with two clients when networking exists, then disconnect immediately before/after a committed result. Query the same command and compare authoritative snapshot/receipt with UI. Restart the relevant zone, reject stale epochs, and rerun the previous phase route. Pure visual/input features instead verify cleanup and unchanged server facts. These are future test recipes, not reported passes.

Tuning, accessibility and observability

First dungeon target 15–25 minutes for four players is a proposal; start with one boss and two encounter rooms. No raids, global matchmaking service or mass concurrency claim.

Record queue/reservation/transfer latency, encounter phase, wipes, reward receipts and checkpoint recovery. Telegraphs include shape/time cues and reduced-flash variants.

Art gaps, production and do-not-build-yet

The asset ZIP and installed PaperZD APIs remain unverified. Required new art/unsupported layer combinations are tracked in art/animation-matrix.html and art/equipment-visual-matrix.html. A legal debug visual can prove authority but is not finished content. Production features listed as later/optional remain disabled until their phase/gate passes.
